script.base: No saved spread or total, so the script is inferred from two-game form only. SF has the more efficient offense (Purdy 8 car/59 rush yds, CMC 20/91 and Kaelon Black 21/90, Evans 10 tgt/103, Kittle 9/92, Samuel 11/79) against an ARI defense that has bled the middle (9.53 YPA on 15 att) and right (8.62 on 24) and allowed 6 runs of 10+. ARI is a Brissett committee (Allgeier 22 car/71, Love 20/70, both under 3.5 YPC) that has been bad vs the blitz (EPA/db -0.31 vs +0.13 with no blitz) while SF blitzes 28%. Base case: SF leads or stays in front in a competitive game, throws into the middle, and keeps splitting carries between CMC and Black; ARI trails and funnels throws to McBride (23 targets/136 yds) rather than feeding the run.
script.flip1: SF's pass rush is short-handed (Bosa, Romello Height, and James Thompson Jr. all Out), so the 28% blitz does not get home, ARI sustains drives, and the game stays close or ARI leads. Both QBs throw; McBride, Kittle, and Samuel become the over paths, and both committees' rush lines stay modest.
script.flip2: SF jumps ahead early and kills the clock with CMC and Black. ARI abandons the run, so Allgeier/Love rush yards die, and a true blowout trims SF starter routes late. That carry bump is the main threat to a CMC rush+rec under; it does not require Kittle to go under unless the game turns into a slog.

injury_fallout: Source is the pre-game nflverse injury report in the pack; practice-trend (DNP/limited/full) and inactives are not saved. SF WR Demarcus Robinson Out (ankle) leaves 6 targets/84 yards/72 air yards from the two-game sample to be redistributed among CMC (already 12 targets), Samuel (11), Evans (10, but Questionable, hip), and Kittle (9). Evans Questionable is unresolved: a limitation helps Kittle/Samuel/CMC; a full Evans day keeps the deep share. SF DE Nick Bosa Out (knee), DE Romello Height Out (hand), and DT James Thompson Jr. Out (ankle) are a pass-rush and interior downgrade, so ARI's -0.31 EPA/db vs blitz may not travel; pack does not say whether those three already sat in SF's two defensive games (3.95 YPC allowed). ARI S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson Out (back) is the coverage loss that helps SF downfield/middle shots; pack does not say if he played in the two games that produced ARI's 9.53 middle YPA. ARI CB Max Melton Questionable (toe) would help outside WRs only if he sits. ARI DT Roy Lopez Questionable (groin) is a mild SF run boost only if inactive. No Doubtful tags.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, MOFO/MOFC, or man/zone rate in the pack. Location YPA is the only shell proxy: ARI middle 9.53 (15 att), right 8.62 (24), left 6.71 (14); SF middle is the tightest zone at 5.75 (8 att), right 7.83 (24), left 6.89 (19).
matchup.pressure: SF blitz rate 28% and ARI EPA/db vs blitz -0.31 vs +0.13 with no blitz, but Bosa, Height, and Thompson are Out so pressure may not arrive. ARI blitzes only 21%; SF EPA/db vs blitz is +0.98 vs +0.38 with no blitz, so SF's offense has thrived when blitzed.
matchup.bleeds: ARI bleeds the middle and the right and has allowed 6 runs of 10+ with a 3.98 rush YPC (ordinary, not a collapse). SF has allowed only 3 runs of 10+, 3.95 rush YPC, and 4/55 on 20+ passes; its softest pass side is right (7.83), not the middle.
matchup.overlap: Kittle (9 targets, 88 air yards, 92 rec yards) is the healthy SF pass-catcher aimed at ARI's middle bleed, with Taylor-Demerson Out as the missing safety. He is not the primary target (CMC 12, Samuel 11, Evans 10). ARI's primary, McBride (23 targets, 125 air yards), runs into SF's tightest zone (middle 5.75), so there is no primary-target overlap for ARI. CMC's under is a carry-split read, not a run-defense bleed (ARI 3.98 YPC, 6 explosives).

form: Two games only (pack weeks 1-2; last4 lists match those totals). ARI: McBride rec 95 then 41; Wilson 56 then 18 on 133 air yards vs 74 rec yards (poor conversion); Bourne 75 then 11; Harrison 33 then 0 on 4 targets/74 air; Allgeier rush 61 then 10 (22/71, 3.23 YPC); Love rush 41 then 29 (20/70); Brissett rush 17 then 7. SF: CMC rush 68 then 23, rec 20 then 43, rush+rec 88 then 66; Black rush 65 then 25 (21/90); Purdy rush 29 then 30 (8/59, 7.4 YPC, treated as fluky efficiency); Samuel rush+rec 60 then 35; Evans 49 then 54, both under 55.5, but Questionable; Kittle 12 then 80; Juszczyk one listed game of 27. No OC/QB change is noted in the pack.

pre_mortem: Monday case against CMC under: the market's 100.5 was the real projection, Black was a two-week change-up, Robinson's targets and an Evans hip limit turned CMC into the offense, and a lead script gave him the 68-rush game plus the 43-rec game in the same afternoon. Monday case against Kittle over: week-1 usage repeated (12 yards), Evans played and won the middle, the 9.53 YPA was already the backup safety, and Kittle saw 3 targets while Samuel and CMC took the Robinson work. Those counters are why both are leans, not strong. They are not stronger than the written reads, so the legs stay flagged for the human rather than cut.
